title: Guard MemoryRegistry.Close() against double-close panic
description:
**Severity: CRITICAL**

**File**: `core/controlplane/scheduler/registry_memory.go:110-113`

**Bug**: `Close()` calls `close(r.stopCh)` with no guard. If called twice, Go panics on closing an already-closed channel. This can happen during error handling or shutdown races.

**Fix**: Add a `sync.Once` to protect the close operation. Replace the bare `close(r.stopCh)` with a `sync.Once`-guarded call.
definitionOfDone: Close() uses sync.Once to prevent double-close panic
Calling Close() twice does not panic
Add a unit test that calls Close() twice and verifies no panic

implementationPlan.description: Add a `closeOnce sync.Once` field to the `MemoryRegistry` struct (registry_memory.go:11-16). The `sync` package is already imported.
Replace the bare `close(r.stopCh)` in `Close()` (line 112) with `r.closeOnce.Do(func() { close(r.stopCh) })`. This makes Close() idempotent — calling it twice is safe.
Add a test `TestMemoryRegistryDoubleCloseNoPanic` in `registry_memory_test.go` that creates a MemoryRegistry, calls Close() twice, and asserts no panic using `require.NotPanics` or a recover guard.
